result.narrative: Boeing's payment behaviour remains clean: no open overdue notifications and only one minor, quickly-cured delay (3 days, $650k) in the last six months against a $9M accepted credit line from TCI. The Watch-band score of 27.8 is driven entirely by negative news flow, chiefly a severity-4 layoffs headline from 3 days ago that leaves open the possibility of further job cuts amid stalled production, corroborated by a second severity-4 layoffs article 14 days prior (5% of commercial airplane workforce) and secondary severity-2 items on 737 Max production delays and DOT/FAA regulatory scrutiny. Positive news (bullish analyst sentiment, $745B backlog, Asia deals, delivery upticks) is present but scored zero and does not offset the layoffs narrative under the model. The recommendation is to maintain the current $9,000,000 limit, as PD (0.1784) sits within the 0.25 appetite target and expected loss is unchanged before and after; the adjudicator agreed with this outcome but flagged caveats, including thin evidentiary detail behind the lead article, low confidence in the payment trend given only one historical data point, and the need to confirm the two layoffs articles are not duplicate reports of the same event. A move to Healthy would require the score to fall 7.8 points, consistent with the current clean payment record aging further and no fresh negative news; conversely, a slide to High Risk would need a 22.2-point rise (score to 50), which could come from new negative news compounding the existing layoffs/production narrative or payment deterioration reaching 33 days past due.
